limits: Early Release draft, raw and unedited; no experiments, numbers are ecosystem counts at time of writing and have dated.
Origin story is secondhand from a Latent Space Podcast interview.
Roots are advisory: spec says servers should, not must, respect them, so roots are not a security control.
Authors/year not printed in the extracted text; some figure numbering is inconsistent (sampling figure referenced as 2-3 but is 2-4; Inspector referenced as 2-7 but captioned 2-5).
practices: Evaluate tool choice accuracy (e.g. with Promptfoo) before and after adding MCP servers, since many tools can degrade accuracy (sidebar Too Many Tools).
Always support the stdio transport; add Streamable HTTP if deploying a remote server or supporting remote servers (sidebar Supporting Multiple Transports).
Do not treat roots as access control; use a proper access control system (The Host Application and MCP Client).
Treat MCP servers as attack surface (e.g. rug pull) and mitigate for local and remote servers (Warning box, The MCP Server).
Treat transports as a security boundary; build a custom transport if security needs exceed built-ins (The MCP Transport).
Transport developers who include authorization must implement OAuth 2.1 (Connection Lifecycle section).
Both client and server must support the optional utilities (cancellation, ping, progress) for them to work (Note box).
